### `discussion_board_guests`

Guest actor table for unauthenticated users identified by session tokens.
This table represents guest users who interact with the system without
formal authentication credentials, tracked through session tokens for
continuity while maintaining the actor pattern consistent with other user
types in the system.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `session_token`
  > Unique session token for guest identification. Used to track guest users
  > across requests without authentication.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the guest account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest account was soft-deleted. Nullable, as guests
  > are not typically deleted.

### `discussion_board_guest_sessions`

Temporary session tokens for guest access without authentication
credentials.

This table stores session records for guest (unauthenticated) users who
access the discussion board without logging in. Guest sessions allow
tracking of anonymous user activity while maintaining security through
session tokens.

## Purpose:
- Track anonymous user sessions and activity
- Maintain session state without requiring authentication
- Support time-limited guest access to the platform

## Key Relationships:
- Belongs to guest users via `guest_id`
- Each guest can have multiple sessions over time
- Sessions are temporary and expire after a period of inactivity

## Security Considerations:
- Sessions expire after a predetermined time
- IP and referrer information is logged for security auditing
- No sensitive user data is stored beyond session metadata

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `guest_id`: Guest user's [discussion_board_guests.id](#discussion_board_guests).
- `ip`: IP address of the guest user when the session was created.
- `href`: Current page URL the guest was accessing when the session started.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL showing how the guest arrived at the site.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the session was created.
- `expired_at`: Timestamp when the session expires and becomes invalid.

### `discussion_board_members`

Member actor table storing authentication credentials and profile
information for registered users who can create articles, comments, and
request administrator privileges.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Member's unique identifier.
- `email`: Unique email address for login. Required field.
- `password_hash`: Securely hashed password for authentication.
- `display_name`: User's display name (1-100 characters). Required field.
- `bio`: User's biography text. Optional field.
- `role`: User's role: guest, member, admin, or superAdmin. Required field.
- `is_banned`: Whether the member account is currently banned.
- `ban_reason`: Reason for banning the member account.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the member account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the member account was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the member account was soft-deleted. Null if active.

### `discussion_board_member_sessions`

JWT session tokens for member authentication with access and refresh
token support.

This table tracks active login sessions for member users, storing JWT
tokens and session metadata.
Sessions are created when members log in and invalidated when they log
out or change their password.

Sessions expire after 30 days of inactivity.

Relationships:
- Belongs to: discussion_board_members (member)
- Session management: Handles login/logout and password change invalidation

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_member_id`: Belonged member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members).
- `access_token`
  > JWT access token for authentication. Short-lived token (15 minutes) used
  > for API requests.
- `refresh_token`
  > JWT refresh token for session continuation. Long-lived token (30 days)
  > used to obtain new access tokens.
- `ip`: IP address of the client when the session was created.
- `referrer`: Referrer header value when the session was created.
- `user_agent`: User agent string from the client browser.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the session was created. Also serves as last activity
  > timestamp.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when the session expires (30 days from created_at). Session
  > becomes invalid after this time.
- `invalidated_at`
  > Timestamp when the session was explicitly invalidated (logout or password
  > change). Null if session is still valid.

### `discussion_board_member_password_resets`

Password reset tokens for member account recovery with expiration. Tracks
reset requests, validates tokens, and records when resets are completed.
Provides security audit trail for password change operations.

## Business Purpose
- Enables secure password recovery for member accounts
- Validates reset tokens with expiration checking
- Records when password resets are completed
- Maintains audit trail for security compliance

## Key Relationships
- Belongs to discussion_board_members (member account)
- One member can have multiple password resets over time
- Used for recovery workflows, not日常 authentication

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_member_id`: Member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members) being reset.
- `token`
  > Unique password reset token for authentication. Used to verify password
  > reset requests securely.
- `expires_at`
  > Expiration time for the password reset token. Tokens must be used before
  > this time to be valid.
- `used_at`
  > Timestamp when the password was successfully reset using this token. Null
  > until reset is completed.
- `ip`: IP address where the password reset request was initiated.
- `href`: Full URL where the password reset request originated.
- `referrer`: Referrer header from the password reset request.
- `created_at`: When the password reset request was created.
- `updated_at`: When the password reset record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for password reset records.

### `discussion_board_admins`

Admin actor table with email/password authentication credentials and
administrative privileges. Admins can create/edit/delete sections, delete
any articles/comments, ban/unban users, and manage administrator
requests.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`: Unique admin email address used for authentication.
- `password_hash`: Hashed password for secure authentication.
- `display_name`: Admin's display name for content attribution (1-100 characters).
- `bio`: Optional biography text for admin profile.
- `is_banned`: Whether this admin account is currently banned.
- `ban_reason`: Reason for admin ban, recorded when is_banned is true.
- `role`
  > Admin role enum: 'admin' for regular administrator, 'super_admin' for
  > super administrator with elevated privileges.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when admin account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when admin account was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Optional timestamp for soft deletion when admin account is removed.

### `discussion_board_admin_sessions`

JWT session tokens for admin authentication with access and refresh token
support.

This table tracks active admin sessions with security-relevant metadata
including IP address, requested URL, and referrer information. Each
session is associated with an admin user and contains both access and
refresh tokens for JWT-based authentication. The session expires after 30
days from last activity, with access tokens valid for 15 minutes and
refresh tokens valid for 30 days.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_admin_id`: Belonged admin's @{link discussion_board_admins.id}.
- `ip`: Client IP address at login time.
- `href`: Requested URL at login time.
- `referrer`: HTTP referrer header at login time.
- `access_token`: JWT access token for authentication (15 minutes expiration).
- `refresh_token`: JWT refresh token for token refresh (30 days expiration).
- `created_at`: Session creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Session last update timestamp.
- `expired_at`: Session expiration timestamp (30 days from creation).

### `discussion_board_admin_password_resets`

Password reset tokens for admin account recovery with expiration. This
table stores one-time use tokens that allow administrators to reset their
passwords when they forget them. Each token is valid for a limited time
and can only be used once.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`: Admin's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins).
- `token`: Unique password reset token.
- `expires_at`: Token expiration timestamp.
- `used_at`: Timestamp when token was used (null if unused).
- `created_at`: Token creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.

### `discussion_board_super_admins`

Super admin actor table with email/password authentication credentials
and full administrative privileges. Stores super administrator account
information, authentication credentials, and profile data. Super admins
have full administrative capabilities including managing other
administrators, sections, and user bans.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`: Super admin's email address for authentication.
- `password_hash`: Hashed password for authentication.
- `display_name`: Super admin's display name for UI presentation.
- `bio`: Super admin's biography or description.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp. Nullable means not deleted.

### `discussion_board_super_admin_sessions`

JWT session tokens for super admin authentication with access and refresh
token support

This table stores authentication sessions for super administrators. Each
session
represents a logged-in state with JWT access and refresh tokens. The table
includes security context information (IP address, referrer, page) for audit
trail purposes and proper session expiration tracking.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_super_admin_id`
  > References the super admin user whose session this represents. {@link
  > discussion_board_super_admins.id}.
- `access_token`: JWT access token for API authentication.
- `refresh_token`: JWT refresh token for session extension.
- `ip`: IP address from which the session was initiated.
- `href`: The page URL where the user landed after authentication.
- `referrer`: The referring page that directed the user to the application.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the session was created.
- `expired_at`: Timestamp when the session expires and becomes invalid.

### `discussion_board_super_admin_password_resets`

Password reset tokens for super admin account recovery with expiration.

This table stores secure password reset tokens for super administrators
who need to recover their account access. Each token is tied to a
specific super admin and has a defined expiration time for security
purposes.

## Usage
- Super administrators can request password resets when they forget their
credentials
- Tokens are generated with cryptographically secure random values
- Tokens expire after a defined period (typically 1 hour)
- Once used, tokens are invalidated to prevent reuse

## Security Considerations
- Tokens should be single-use and invalidated immediately after
successful password reset
- Token generation should use cryptographically secure random values
- Expired tokens should be automatically cleaned up
- Multiple concurrent reset requests may be allowed but old tokens should
be invalidated

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `super_admin_id`
  > Super admin account requesting password reset. {@link
  > discussion_board_super_admins.id}.
- `token`: Secure password reset token generated for authentication.
- `expires_at`: Token expiration timestamp. Tokens are valid until this time.
- `created_at`: When this password reset record was created.
- `updated_at`: When this password reset record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: When this password reset record was deleted (soft delete). Null if active.

### `discussion_board_administrator_requests`

User applications for elevated administrator privileges with status
tracking.

This table stores administrator privilege requests submitted by members
who want to become administrators.
Each request includes a reason text explaining the user's qualification
and motivation.

Key characteristics:
- Only members (regular users) can submit administrator requests
- Requests follow a status workflow: pending → approved or rejected
- Super administrators can approve requests to grant administrator
privileges
- Self-protection prevents users from approving their own requests
- A user can have only one active (pending) request at a time
- All requests are visible to super administrators for review

Relationships:
- Belongs to discussion_board_members (the requesting user)
- Optionally processed by discussion_board_super_admins (the approving
super admin)

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `submitter_member_id`
  > User who submitted the administrator request. {@link

- `processed_by_super_admin_id`

  > [discussion_board_super_admins.id](#discussion_board_super_admins).
- `reason`

  > non-empty.
- `status`

- `processed_at`

reasons. Banned users cannot log in but their existing content remains
visible. This is a primary table with full CRUD operations for
administrative workflows.

- `discussion_board_member_id`: The user being banned. [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members).

## Sections
- Get all sections (GET /sections)

- Delete section (DELETE /sections/:id) - Admin only

## Articles

- Get comments for article (GET /articles/:id/comments)

## Administrator System

- Search tags by prefix (GET /tags/search)

operations.description:
## Guest Session Join Operation

This operation creates a new guest session for unauthenticated users accessing the discussion board. Guest users don't have credentials like passwords - they access the system anonymously through temporary session tokens.

### Purpose and Functionality

The join operation initializes a new guest session by:
1. Creating a new record in the `discussion_board_guests` table with a unique session token
2. Setting up an initial session in `discussion_board_guest_sessions` with connection metadata
3. Generating both access and refresh tokens for the guest session
4. Returning session information including token expiration times

### Database Implementation

The operation involves:
- Inserting into `discussion_board_guests` table with auto-generated UUID and session token
- Inserting into `discussion_board_guest_sessions` table with connection metadata (IP, referrer, href)
- Setting `expired_at` timestamp based on session timeout policy (typically 30 minutes)
- Storing `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps in UTC format
- The `deleted_at` field remains null as guest sessions are not typically soft-deleted

### Security Considerations

- Session tokens must be cryptographically secure random strings
- IP addresses are stored for security auditing purposes
- Referrer and href tracking helps understand user acquisition sources
- Sessions automatically expire after the timeout period
- No sensitive user data is stored in guest sessions

### Request Requirements

The request may optionally include:
- IP address (extracted from request headers if not provided)
- Referrer URL (from HTTP referer header)
- Current page href (from request context)

### Response Structure

The response returns an `IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized` object containing:
- Access token for immediate authentication
- Refresh token for session renewal
- Token expiration timestamps
- Session metadata including guest ID and session token

responseBody.description: Authorized guest session with access and refresh tokens

operations.description:
## Guest Session Refresh Operation

This operation renews an existing guest session by validating the current session token and issuing new access and refresh tokens with updated expiration times.

### Purpose and Functionality

The refresh operation extends guest session validity by:
1. Validating the current session token against `discussion_board_guest_sessions` table
2. Checking that the session hasn't already expired (expired_at > current time)
3. Updating session metadata (updated_at timestamp)
4. Generating new access and refresh tokens
5. Extending the session expiration time

### Database Implementation

The operation involves:
- Querying `discussion_board_guest_sessions` table by session token
- Verifying `expired_at` timestamp is still in the future
- Updating `updated_at` timestamp on the session record
- Optionally updating IP address or referrer if significant changes detected
- Generating new tokens and extending `expired_at` by session timeout period
- The `discussion_board_guests` table's `updated_at` field is also refreshed

### Security Considerations

- Session tokens must be validated before renewal
- Sessions cannot be refreshed after expiration
- Large time gaps between refresh requests may require re-authentication
- Suspicious IP changes between refreshes may trigger security checks
- No sensitive data exposure in the refresh response

### Request Requirements

The request must include:
- Current session token (usually in Authorization header)
- Optional: IP address for validation against stored session

### Response Structure

The response returns an `IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized` object containing:
- New access token with extended validity
- New refresh token (token rotation for security)
- Updated expiration timestamps
- Current session metadata

1. Validating the current session token against `discussion_board_guest_sessions` table
2. Checking that the session hasn't already expired (expired_at > current time)
3. Updating session metadata (updated_at timestamp)
4. Generating new access and refresh tokens
5. Extending the session expiration time

### Database Implementation

The operation involves:
- Querying `discussion_board_guest_sessions` table by session token
- Verifying `expired_at` timestamp is still in the future
- Updating `updated_at` timestamp on the session record
- Optionally updating IP address or referrer if significant changes detected
- Generating new tokens and extending `expired_at` by session timeout period
- The `discussion_board_guests` table's `updated_at` field is also refreshed

### Security Considerations

- Session tokens must be validated before renewal
- Sessions cannot be refreshed after expiration
- Large time gaps between refresh requests may require re-authentication
- Suspicious IP changes between refreshes may trigger security checks
- No sensitive data exposure in the refresh response

### Request Requirements

The request must include:
- Current session token (usually in Authorization header)
- Optional: IP address for validation against stored session

### Response Structure

The response returns an `IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized` object containing:
- New access token with extended validity
- New refresh token (token rotation for security)
- Updated expiration timestamps
- Current session metadata

- The ban record's `deleted_at` timestamp is set to the current timestamp

- All previous content remains intact and accessible

- Only super administrators can unban users

- Unban actions are logged with timestamp and administrator reference
- Banned users cannot unban themselves

text: I'll generate comprehensive E2E test functions for your Economic/Political Discussion Board API. Based on the API interface specification that has been created, I'll now call the test agent to create thorough test coverage for all endpoints.

instruction:
Create comprehensive E2E test functions for the Economic/Political Discussion Board API based on the interface specification.

## Test Coverage Requirements

### Authentication & Authorization Tests
- User registration with valid and invalid data
- User login with correct and incorrect credentials
- Password change for authenticated users
- Profile retrieval for current user
- Authentication refresh mechanism
- Authorization checks for admin-only endpoints

### User Profile Tests
- Retrieve user profiles by ID
- Update current user profile information
- Delete user accounts and verify cascade deletion of related articles and comments
- Profile visibility (users can view other users' profiles)

### Section Tests
- Get all sections
- Get section by ID
- Create, update, and delete sections (admin-only)
- Section permission checks (regular users cannot modify sections)

### Article Tests
- Create articles in sections with valid and invalid data
- Retrieve articles in sections with pagination
- Get individual article details
- Update articles (author-only or admin)
- Delete articles (author-only or admin)
- Upload and download attachments
- Search articles by title/content with pagination
- Tag filtering for articles
- Sorting functionality (newest/oldest first)

### Comment Tests
- Create comments on articles
- Retrieve comments for articles (sorted by oldest first)
- Update comments (author-only or admin)
- Delete comments (author-only or admin)
- Comment count accuracy in article listings

### Administrator Tests
- Get pending administrator requests
- Create administrator requests with reasons
- Approve/reject administrator requests (super admin only)
- Promote/demote administrator roles (super admin only)
- Ban/unban users with reasons
- Get banned users list
- Verify banned users cannot log in but their content remains visible

### Tag Tests
- Retrieve popular tags
- Search tags by prefix

## Test Structure Requirements
- Use Jest testing framework
- Implement proper test organization by feature modules
- Include setup and teardown for test data
- Mock external dependencies (file storage, email services)
- Implement proper test data factories for creating test entities
- Include error handling tests for all endpoints
- Test edge cases (empty lists, pagination boundaries, invalid IDs)
- Verify proper HTTP status codes for all scenarios
- Include performance tests for search functionality with large datasets
- Test concurrent operations (multiple users creating/updating same resources)
- Validate input sanitization and XSS prevention

Test scenario for super administrator retrieving detailed information about an administrator request.

## Test Steps
1. Join as super admin actor
2. Join as member actor (to create administrator request)
3. Member submits an administrator request with a reason
4. Super admin approves the administrator request

   - Timestamps (submitted_at, processed_at)
   - Rejection reason is null for approved requests

- HTTP 200 status code for successful retrieval
- Response structure matches IDiscussionBoardAdministratorRequest schema
- Submitter information is properly joined from discussion_board_members
- Processor information is properly joined from discussion_board_super_admins
- All timestamps are present and correctly formatted
- Status transitions are properly recorded (approved status with processor info)

## Edge Case
Test with a pending administrator request that has not been processed yet to verify:
- Processor field is null
- processed_at field is null
- rejection_reason field is null

2. **Create Test Ban Records**:
   - Join as regular member and get member ID
   - Create multiple ban records with different statuses (active/inactive) using `/discussionBoard/admin/bans`
   - Ensure at least 5-10 ban records exist for pagination testing

3. **Test Default Pagination**:
   - Call `/discussionBoard/admin/bans` with no filters
   - Verify response contains default page (page 1) with default limit (100)
   - Verify records are sorted by banned_at descending (most recent first)
   - Verify pagination metadata (current, limit, records, pages)

4. **Test Custom Pagination**:
   - Request page 2 with limit 5
   - Verify only 5 records returned
   - Verify current page is 2
   - Verify total records count matches expected
   - Verify records on page 2 are different from page 1

5. **Test User ID Filter**:
   - Filter by specific user ID
   - Verify only ban records for that user returned
   - Verify no records for other users in response

6. **Test Administrator ID Filter**:
   - Filter by administrator ID who created bans
   - Verify only ban records created by that admin returned
   - Verify no records from other admins in response

7. **Test Date Range Filter**:
   - Filter by date range (e.g., last 7 days)
   - Verify only records within date range returned
   - Verify records with banned_at outside range excluded

8. **Test Active Status Filter**:
   - Filter by active bans only (unbanned_at is null)
   - Verify only currently active ban records returned
   - Verify no unbanned records in response

9. **Test Inactive Status Filter**:
   - Filter by inactive bans only (unbanned_at is not null)
   - Verify only unbanned records returned
   - Verify no active bans in response

10. **Test Combined Filters**:
    - Combine multiple filters (user ID + date range + active status)
    - Verify all filter conditions are applied with AND logic
    - Verify only records matching all criteria returned

11. **Test Boundary Conditions**:
    - Request page 0 (should be rejected or treated as page 1)
    - Request limit 0 (should be rejected or default limit applied)
    - Request limit 100 (should be capped at maximum allowed)
    - Request page beyond available pages (should return empty array)

12. **Test Authorization**:
    - Attempt to call endpoint as guest (should return 401)
    - Attempt to call endpoint as regular member (should return 403)

## Validation Points

- Proper pagination metadata in all responses
- Correct sorting (banned_at descending by default)
- Accurate filtering for each filter parameter
- Proper handling of null values (active vs inactive bans)
- Correct date range filtering with timezone handling
- Authorization enforcement (only admins can access)
- Error handling for invalid parameters
- Performance with large datasets

scenario.draft:
Test scenario for ban record data integrity and consistency. This scenario validates that the ban record listing endpoint returns accurate and consistent data, properly handles edge cases, and maintains referential integrity.

## Test Steps

1. **Setup**: Join as admin actor using `/discussionBoard/auth/admin/join`

2. **Create Clean Test Data**:
   - Join as member and record member ID
   - Create ban record with specific reason and timestamp
   - Unban the user to create inactive ban record
   - Verify both active and inactive records exist

3. **Test User Reference Integrity**:
   - Create ban record with valid user ID
   - Verify ban record returned includes complete user summary
   - Test ban record with non-existent user ID (should handle gracefully)
   - Verify user display_name and bio correctly populated

4. **Test Administrator Reference Integrity**:
   - Create ban record with admin's ID (from JWT context)
   - Verify ban record includes correct admin summary
   - Verify admin display_name and role are accurate
   - Test that no unauthorized admin data leaks

5. **Test Ban Reason Storage and Retrieval**:
   - Create ban with specific reason text
   - Verify exact reason text returned in ban record
   - Test with special characters and Unicode
   - Test with very long reason text (1000+ characters)

6. **Test Timestamp Consistency**:
   - Verify banned_at timestamp matches server time
   - Verify unbanned_at timestamp matches unban action
   - Test timestamp timezone handling (UTC)
   - Verify timestamps in correct ISO format

7. **Test Null Value Handling**:
   - Verify active ban has null unbanned_at
   - Verify inactive ban has non-null unbanned_at
   - Test filtering by null/unnull unbanned_at
   - Verify API handles null fields correctly

8. **Test Pagination Consistency**:
   - Create many ban records (50+)
   - Paginate through all records
   - Verify no duplicate records across pages
   - Verify no missing records across pages
   - Verify total count matches actual record count

9. **Test Filtering Consistency**:
   - Apply filter and get record count
   - Get records with same filter
   - Verify record count matches data array length
   - Test with multiple filter combinations
   - Verify AND logic between filters

10. **Test Concurrent Operations**:
    - Create ban records from multiple sessions
    - Query ban records immediately after creation
    - Verify all records appear in listings
    - Test race conditions with pagination
    - Verify data consistency under load

11. **Test Authorization and Access Control**:
    - Verify only admin users can access endpoint
    - Test guest users get unauthorized error
    - Test regular members get forbidden error
    - Verify admin role hierarchy (super admin can also access)

12. **Test Response Format Consistency**:
    - Verify pagination structure is consistent
    - Verify data array format is consistent
    - Verify error responses follow expected format
    - Test content-type headers are correct

## Validation Points

- Accurate user and administrator references
- Consistent timestamp handling and storage
- Proper null value management
- Data integrity across pagination
- Filtering accuracy and consistency
- Authorization enforcement
- Response format standardization
- Error handling for missing references
- Performance and reliability under concurrent access

text: I'll implement the API functions for your Economic/Political Discussion Board. Based on the current state, I can see that the analyze, database, interface, and test agents have been successfully executed, and now it's time to implement the business logic with the realize agent.

instruction:
Implement business logic for the Economic/Political Discussion Board API based on the interface specification.

## Implementation Requirements

### Authentication & Authorization Services
- Implement JWT-based authentication with refresh tokens
- Password hashing using bcrypt
- User registration validation and email confirmation
- Role-based authorization checks (regular user, administrator, super administrator)
- Authentication middleware and guards for NestJS

### User Profile Services
- User CRUD operations with proper validation
- Profile picture management
- Implementation of cascade deletion for user's articles and comments
- User banning functionality with reason tracking

### Section Services
- CRUD operations for sections (admin-only)
- Section permission validation
- Section usage count (number of articles in each section)

### Article Services
- Article creation with title, content, section assignment, and tags
- File upload handling for attachments and images
- Article retrieval with pagination and sorting
- Search functionality with full-text search capabilities
- Tag management and filtering
- Article update and deletion with authorization checks

### Comment Services
- Comment creation, retrieval, update, and deletion
- Single-level comment implementation (no nested replies)
- Comment count tracking in articles
- Comment ordering by creation date (oldest first)

### Administrator Services
- Administrator request handling (create, approve, reject)
- Administrator role management (promote, demote)
- Permission validation for admin operations
- Admin activity logging

### Banning System
- User banning/unbanning functionality
- Ban reason storage and retrieval
- Banned user access restrictions (prevent login while preserving content)

### File Services
- Secure file upload and storage handling
- File type validation
- File download with proper headers
- Attachment management for articles

### Testing Integration
- All services must pass existing E2E tests
- Implement proper error handling that matches test expectations
- Database transaction support for data consistency
- Implement proper validation pipes for all DTOs

### Code Quality Requirements
- TypeScript strict mode compliance
- Follow NestJS best practices and patterns
- Implement proper dependency injection
- Include comprehensive JSDoc comments
- Handle all edge cases identified in E2E tests
- Implement proper database transactions
- Optimize database queries (eager loading where appropriate)

import { TypedBody, TypedRoute } from "@nestia/core";
import { Controller, Ip } from "@nestjs/common";
import typia from "typia";

import { IDiscussionBoardGuest } from "../../../../api/structures/IDiscussionBoardGuest";
import { postDiscussionBoardAuthGuestJoin } from "../../../../providers/postDiscussionBoardAuthGuestJoin";
import { postDiscussionBoardAuthGuestRefresh } from "../../../../providers/postDiscussionBoardAuthGuestRefresh";

@Controller("/discussionBoard/auth/guest")
export class DiscussionboardAuthGuestController {
  /**
   * ## Guest Session Join Operation
   *
   * This operation creates a new guest session for unauthenticated users accessing the discussion board. Guest users don't have credentials like passwords - they access the system anonymously through temporary session tokens.
   *
   * ### Purpose and Functionality
   *
   * The join operation initializes a new guest session by:
   * 1. Creating a new record in the `discussion_board_guests` table with a unique session token
   * 2. Setting up an initial session in `discussion_board_guest_sessions` with connection metadata
   * 3. Generating both access and refresh tokens for the guest session
   * 4. Returning session information including token expiration times
   *
   * ### Database Implementation
   *
   * The operation involves:
   * - Inserting into `discussion_board_guests` table with auto-generated UUID and session token
   * - Inserting into `discussion_board_guest_sessions` table with connection metadata (IP, referrer, href)
   * - Setting `expired_at` timestamp based on session timeout policy (typically 30 minutes)
   * - Storing `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps in UTC format
   * - The `deleted_at` field remains null as guest sessions are not typically soft-deleted
   *
   * ### Security Considerations
   *
   * - Session tokens must be cryptographically secure random strings
   * - IP addresses are stored for security auditing purposes
   * - Referrer and href tracking helps understand user acquisition sources
   * - Sessions automatically expire after the timeout period
   * - No sensitive user data is stored in guest sessions
   *
   * ### Request Requirements
   *
   * The request may optionally include:
   * - IP address (extracted from request headers if not provided)
   * - Referrer URL (from HTTP referer header)
   * - Current page href (from request context)
   *
   * ### Response Structure
   *
   * The response returns an `IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized` object containing:
   * - Access token for immediate authentication
   * - Refresh token for session renewal
   * - Token expiration timestamps
   * - Session metadata including guest ID and session token
   *
   * @setHeader token.access Authorization
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Request body for creating a new guest session
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type join
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor guest
   * @x-autobe-specification Create new guest session by generating session token and storing initial session metadata (IP address, referrer, current page). Returns the session token and expiration information.
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Post("join")
  public async join(
    @Ip()
    ip: string,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IDiscussionBoardGuest.IJoin,
  ): Promise<IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized> {
    try {
      return await postDiscussionBoardAuthGuestJoin({
        ip,
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * ## Guest Session Refresh Operation
   *
   * This operation renews an existing guest session by validating the current session token and issuing new access and refresh tokens with updated expiration times.
   *
   * ### Purpose and Functionality
   *
   * The refresh operation extends guest session validity by:
   * 1. Validating the current session token against `discussion_board_guest_sessions` table
   * 2. Checking that the session hasn't already expired (expired_at > current time)
   * 3. Updating session metadata (updated_at timestamp)
   * 4. Generating new access and refresh tokens
   * 5. Extending the session expiration time
   *
   * ### Database Implementation
   *
   * The operation involves:
   * - Querying `discussion_board_guest_sessions` table by session token
   * - Verifying `expired_at` timestamp is still in the future
   * - Updating `updated_at` timestamp on the session record
   * - Optionally updating IP address or referrer if significant changes detected
   * - Generating new tokens and extending `expired_at` by session timeout period
   * - The `discussion_board_guests` table's `updated_at` field is also refreshed
   *
   * ### Security Considerations
   *
   * - Session tokens must be validated before renewal
   * - Sessions cannot be refreshed after expiration
   * - Large time gaps between refresh requests may require re-authentication
   * - Suspicious IP changes between refreshes may trigger security checks
   * - No sensitive data exposure in the refresh response
   *
   * ### Request Requirements
   *
   * The request must include:
   * - Current session token (usually in Authorization header)
   * - Optional: IP address for validation against stored session
   *
   * ### Response Structure
   *
   * The response returns an `IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized` object containing:
   * - New access token with extended validity
   * - New refresh token (token rotation for security)
   * - Updated expiration timestamps
   * - Current session metadata
   *
   * @setHeader token.access Authorization
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Request body for refreshing guest session
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type refresh
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor guest
   * @x-autobe-specification Renew guest session by validating current session token and issuing new tokens with extended expiration time.
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Post("refresh")
  public async refresh(
    @TypedBody()
    body: IDiscussionBoardGuest.IRefresh,
  ): Promise<IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized> {
    try {
      return await postDiscussionBoardAuthGuestRefresh({
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }
}
